title: Come, Let Us Join Our Souls to God
description: Come, Let Us Join Our Souls to God in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 52 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Mutual Invitation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, let us join our souls to God In ev-er-last-ing bands, And seize the bless-ings he be-stows With ea-ger hearts and hands.

lines: Come, let us join our souls to God
And seize the blessings he bestows
Come, let us to his temple haste,
Come, let us share, without delay,
Nor shall the years of distant life
O, may our children ever haste
Nor e'er forsake the happy path

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
